note: The order to learn this in. A stage unlocks when the previous one reaches 90% over at least 10 attempts. Scopes are pools, not restrictions on the reference view.

stages.title: a-stem masculine · first cases
stages.why: The base pattern. Ten stems share it, so getting this right unlocks the largest block of the language.

stages.title: a-stem masculine · full grid
stages.why: Adds dative, ablative, genitive, locative, vocative. The dative -āya and genitive -asya are the two you will meet most.

stages.title: a-stem neuter
stages.why: Only three slots differ from the masculine: nom, acc and voc. Learn the contrast, not a new table.

stages.title: long -ā feminine
stages.why: The yā-ādeśa: sītayā, sītāyai, sītāyāḥ. One rule explains the whole family.

stages.title: -i and -u masculine
stages.why: New stem class: guṇa before ṅ-endings gives agneḥ, guroḥ. Same rule, two vowels.

stages.title: long -ī and -ū feminine
stages.why: ī and ū shorten to y and v before vowels: nadyā, vadhvā.

stages.title: -ṛ agent nouns
stages.why: Kinship and agent nouns. Strong ṛ in the nominative: pitā, but pitrā, pitre, pituḥ.

stages.title: consonant stems · -an and -in
stages.why: The n assimilates: rājā, rājñā, rājñaḥ. sukhin is the adjective that makes agreement work.

stages.title: consonant stems · the rest
stages.why: Participles, honorifics and the two odd sibilant stems. After this you have seen every family.

stages.title: irregular: go
stages.why: One stem that follows no other. Learn it as a set of six forms and stop worrying.

stages.sub: mixed stems, one case at a time
stages.title: cases across every family
stages.why: Now the point is the case, not the family: what does genitive mean, and what does it look like everywhere?

stages.title: present tense · singular
stages.why: The base paradigm: -mi, -si, -ti. Everything else is built on recognising these endings.

stages.title: present tense · full
stages.why: Dual and plural endings, plus the -aya- and -nā- classes appearing across roots.

stages.title: past (imperfect)
stages.why: One prefix explains it: the augment a- in front of the present stem.

stages.title: future
stages.why: -sya- plus guṇa. Predictable once the present stem is known.

stages.title: imperative and optative
stages.why: Commands and wishes. Different endings, same roots — this is where the endings stop feeling like a list.

stages.sub: name the tense from the form
stages.title: all tenses mixed
stages.why: Recognition across the whole system: given any form, say what it is doing and to whom.
